Usage: dust [OPTIONS] [PATH]...

Arguments:
  [PATH]...

Options:
  -d, --depth <DEPTH>
          Depth to show

  -T, --threads <THREADS>
          Number of threads to use

      --config <FILE>
          Specify a config file to use

  -n, --number-of-lines <NUMBER>
          Display the 'n' largest entries. (Default is terminal_height)

  -p, --full-paths
          Subdirectories will not have their path shortened

  -X, --ignore-directory <PATH>
          Exclude any file or directory with this path

  -I, --ignore-all-in-file <FILE>
          Exclude any file or directory with a regex matching that listed in this file, the file entries will be added to the ignore regexs provided by --invert_filter

  -L, --dereference-links
          dereference sym links - Treat sym links as directories and go into them

  -x, --limit-filesystem
          Only count the files and directories on the same filesystem as the supplied directory

  -s, --apparent-size
          Use file length instead of blocks

  -r, --reverse
          Print tree upside down (biggest highest)

  -c, --no-colors
          No colors will be printed (Useful for commands like: watch)

          Force colors print

message.content:
Yes — `dust` can ignore `.venv` at any depth via its regex filter flag.

## Use `-v` / `--invert-filter`

```xonsh
dust -v "(/|^)\.venv/" .
```

or simply (matches any path containing `.venv` as a segment):

```xonsh
dust -v "\.venv" .
```

Both hide **top-level** and **nested** `.venv` dirs. Since `-v` takes a regex, use `\` to escape the dot (`\.venv`).

## Why not `-X`?

`-X` / `--ignore-directory` only excludes one **exact path** (e.g. `-X ./foo/.venv`), so it won't catch nested `.venv` directories automatically. The regex `-v` is the right tool here.

## Quick tip: put it in a config file

If you always want this (not just for `.venv` but also e.g. `node_modules`, `__pycache__`), set it once in `dust`'s config so you don't retype it:

```xonsh
dust --config ~/.config/dust/config.toml
```

or a per-project alias:

```xonsh
alias ddust "dust -v '\.venv'"
```

For **your** shell right now, the command to run is:

```
dust -v "\.venv" .
```
